reader.requirement: At 85, when a relative file is not in an open mode (never opened, after a failed OPEN, after CLOSE), every statement that references it other than OPEN and SORT/MERGE USING/GIVING must not execute its operation: READ and START answer 47, WRITE 48, REWRITE and DELETE 49, CLOSE 42, nothing changes in the file, and the AT END / INVALID KEY imperatives do not run; SORT/MERGE USING/GIVING may reference it.

edition-consulted.switches: InForce (Year < 2002): at 85 a READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE/START without AT END/INVALID KEY and no applicable USE is refused (COBOL6826); compile-time only, the runtime statement is the same code
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility (2002+): at 85 every OPEN takes the AllOther file lock and Table 19 is not consulted; no effect on open-mode or position rules

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/IsActive/CobolVersion over Runtime/IO FileConnector, KeyedConnector, RelativeConnector, FileRegistry: the open-mode guards consult no edition; the only edition reads on the path are the sharing default at OPEN and RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError (key<1 only, not reached by this rule).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the six probes print identically at --std 2023; only the compile-time exception-phrase requirement differs
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf24_07 exercises SORT USING/GIVING on a closed file and START after CLOSE; never-opened READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE/START/CLOSE, the sequential-access file, and statements after a failed OPEN are not exercised

probes.printed: never opened: dynamic READ random 47, READ NEXT 47, WRITE 48, REWRITE 49, DELETE 49, START 47, CLOSE 42; sequential-access Q (USE ran each time) 47/48/49/49/42; after failed OPEN INPUT 35: READ 47, WRITE 48, CLOSE 42; after failed OPEN I-O 35: DELETE 49; after CLOSE 47/48/49/49/47/42; reopen reads ABCD; no AT END/INVALID KEY imperative ran (MATCH)
probes.expected: 1985 VIII.1.3.4 statuses 47/48/49/42 for a file not open; the record written before CLOSE intact

OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.4  the text is in the rule (or the clause): "A CLOSE statement is attempted for a file not in the open mode"

reader.notes: Openness is one bit (FileConnector.IsOpen) cleared by every CLOSE and never set by a failed OPEN, and every verb's guard tests it before touching the store. The 4x statuses are logic errors so the conditional imperatives are skipped, matching 1985 VIII.1.3.4; continuing afterwards is the implementor's choice.

No AT END/INVALID KEY imperative ran on any refused statement; only the USE procedure ran. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR3 'no statement may be executed which references the file'; OK §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR17 'as if a separate OPEN statement had been written for each file-name'; OK §1985:VIII.1.3.4 (GRL2.4d) 'an OPEN statement is attempted on a file previously closed with lock'.
